newsitem.title: SPAIN: Guatemala expects China to lift UN veto on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala expects China to lift UN veto on Monday.

text.p: Guatemalan President Alvaro Arzu said on Sunday China could lift on Monday its veto on sending a peacekeeping mission to Guatemala.

China vetoed a resolution before the U.N. Security Council last week to send 155 military observers to Guatemala to monitor U.N.-brokered peace agreements that ended more than three decades of civil war. The 14 other council members supported the resolution.

"We believe that there will be a positive decision on Monday on this subject, as a result of negotiations and not as a result of pressure of any kind," Arzu told a news conference in Madrid during a European trip.
China has vetoed the move because of Guatemala's diplomatic ties with Taiwan, which Beijing considers a renegade province.

Guatemalan and Chinese diplomats in the United States held talks on Wednesday and Thursday in an effort to repair the rift. On Friday, Guatemalan rebel leaders also went to New York to lobby China into approving the mission.
"On Monday the case will once again be presented to the Security Council and there will be a favourable outcome," Guatemalan Foreign Minister Eduardo Stein said at the news conference.

The diplomatic spat has been the only hitch so far in the peace process since the Guatemalan government and leftist guerrillas of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) signed a peace treaty on December 29.
